item.title: Warm Music for Morning Tips

turns.text: Add some warm, hopeful music to this clip, nothing too energetic. Keep the whole video and my voice.

item.tests: Tests whether the delivered video adds music matching an explicit mood while preserving the source footage and speech.

answer_sheet.Music mood: Warm and hopeful, with gentle energy rather than a driving beat.
answer_sheet.Footage and length: Use the entire attached 10-second clip without changing its visuals or timing.
answer_sheet.Original audio: Keep my original voice audible and understandable.
answer_sheet.Platform, framing, and added text: Keep the original framing. No added text; no particular platform.

must_haves: The output contains the full original 10-second kitchen-table video, with no new shots or altered playback speed.
Added music is clearly audible and has a warm, hopeful, gentle character rather than an aggressive or high-energy feel.
The woman's original spoken introduction remains audible and understandable throughout.
The added music ends with the video rather than continuing over extra footage or a blank screen.

turns.text: Could you add some music to the clip I've attached? I've been going back and forth about asking for help with this because I tend to overthink these little things. Please keep the whole video and my voice. For the music, I mean something warm and hopeful, but nothing too energetic. I'm excited to see how it feels with music underneath it.

dialog.agent:
I can't put music under your clip with the tools I have here. I want to be clear about that before spending any of your credits.

**Why:** Nothing I can use here will mix a new music track into an existing video and keep the voice. My tools can make a music track on its own, or edit and join videos, but none of them layers audio underneath. The music-mixing step I do have only works on videos I generate from scratch, not on clips you upload. I also tried to read your clip's length, and the tool couldn't open your uploaded file, so I don't know how long it is yet.

**What I can do:** I can make a warm, hopeful, low-energy instrumental track the same length as your clip. Your video and voice stay exactly as they are. You'd then put the track under your clip in any basic editor (CapCut, iMovie, Clipchamp and others all work) and turn the music down so your voice stays clear. It costs 1 credit per second of music, and tracks can be 15 seconds to 5 minutes long.

If you'd like that, tell me:
1. **How long is the clip?** Then the music will match it.
2. **Any instrument preferences?** If not, I'll use something like soft piano with gentle strings and a slow, warm feel.

You weren't overthinking this. It's a reasonable request, and the only problem is that my tools can't mix the music in.
dialog.why: The reply says the requested job, mixing music under the user's uploaded clip, can't be done with the available tools. Its questions only set up a fallback offer (a separate music track), so the main message is an inability statement rather than a request for details on the original task.
dialog.user: Oh, please just go ahead and try it anyway. I'd rather have something than nothing, and I know the free plan has its limits, that's fine by me.

turns.agent:
I tried, but your account doesn't have enough credits to make any music right now, so I have nothing to send you.

I asked for a 60-second track first, since longer music can always be cut to fit. When the account refused that, I tried a 15-second track, which is the shortest length it can make. That was refused for the same reason. Neither attempt made anything.

Even with credits, the music would come as a separate track, not mixed into your clip. You'd still need to put it under your video yourself in an editor like CapCut, iMovie or Clipchamp.

**What would get you there:**
- **Once you have more credits** (after they refill, or if you buy a credit pack), just say "try again." I'll use the same settings: soft piano and warm strings, slow and calm, no vocals, quiet enough to sit under your voice. Music costs 1 credit per second, so it helps to know your clip's length so I don't make more than you need.
- **If you'd rather not wait,** CapCut, iMovie and Clipchamp all have free music libraries. Searching for something like "warm piano," "hopeful ambient" or "gentle acoustic" should turn up something close, and you can lay it under your clip and lower its volume there.

I'm sorry I couldn't get you a track this time.
